title: Myelodysplastic Syndromes
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE Navigator (NCCN Guidelines Version 3.2026)
provenanceNote: Comprehensive NCCN Guidelines Version 3.2026 clinical navigator for Myelodysplastic Syndromes (MDS). Covers complete clinical algorithm: Diagnostic Workup (CBC with peripheral blood smear, bone marrow aspirate and biopsy with Prussian blue iron stain for ring sideroblasts, conventional cytogenetics/karyotype, comprehensive myeloid NGS covering SF3B1, TP53 multi-hit, ASXL1, RUNX1, STAG2, U2AF1, SRSF2, EZH2, serum erythropoietin EPO level, ferritin, B12/folate) -> Prognostic Risk Stratification (IPSS-M Molecular IPSS and IPSS-R: Very Low, Low, Intermediate, High, Very High) -> Lower-Risk MDS (IPSS-M Very Low / Low / Moderate-Low, IPSS-R <=3.5): Isolated del(5q) -> Lenalidomide 10 mg daily (Category 1 Preferred); Non-del(5q) with symptomatic anemia and serum EPO <=500 mU/mL -> Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs: Epoetin alfa or Darbepoetin alfa); Non-del(5q) transfusion-dependent anemia with ring sideroblasts (>=15% or >=5% with SF3B1 mutation) or ESA refractory -> Luspatercept 1.0-1.75 mg/kg SC q3w (COMMANDS Category 1 Preferred); ESA-refractory transfusion-dependent with high baseline transfusion burden -> Imetelstat (IMerge trial) or Hypomethylating Agent (HMA: Azacitidine, Decitabine) -> Higher-Risk MDS (IPSS-M Moderate-High / High / Very High, IPSS-R >3.5): Evaluation for Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation (HCT, only curative modality); Bridging / Non-transplant therapy with Hypomethylating Agents: Azacitidine 75 mg/m2 SC/IV daily x 7 days q28d (aml-azacitidine Category 1 with demonstrated OS benefit), Decitabine 20 mg/m2 IV daily x 5 days, or Oral Decitabine/Cedazuridine (Inqovi); Relapsed / Refractory -> Clinical trial (HMA + Venetoclax) or intensive AML-like induction. References StewardMD Standard Protocols. DRAFT - clinical decision support; physician decides and dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
sourceNote: Structured in accordance with NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology (NCCN Guidelines) for Myelodysplastic Syndromes Version 3.2026 (July 2026).

a.text: IPSS-M (Molecular IPSS) integrates 31-gene mutation data with cytogenetics, blasts, hemoglobin, platelets, and neutrophils into six risk groups (Very Low, Low, Moderate-Low, Moderate-High, High, Very High); TP53 multi-hit (biallelic) status is the strongest adverse lesion and must be established before treatment planning.

b.text: Serum EPO must be drawn before red cell transfusions; an EPO level above 500 mU/mL predicts poor ESA response, and ESA therapy is not indicated in that setting.

c.text: Allogeneic HCT is the only curative modality for MDS; HLA typing and donor search should begin at diagnosis for all higher-risk and fit patients, and bridging HMA aims to reduce marrow blasts below 5% before transplant.

nodes.name: Workup
nodes.title: MDS: diagnostic workup
nodes.description: Confirm MDS diagnosis and gather the morphology, cytogenetic, molecular, and laboratory data that drive IPSS-M/IPSS-R risk stratification.
bullets: Complete blood count (CBC) with differential, reticulocyte count, and manual peripheral blood smear review for dysplastic morphology in >=1 cell lineages (erythroid, myeloid, megakaryocytic).
Bone marrow aspirate and core biopsy: bone marrow cellularity, myeloid:erythroid ratio, megakaryocyte morphology, and blast percentage count (200 cells on aspirate, 500 on biopsy).
Prussian blue iron stain: mandatory quantification of ring sideroblasts (>=15% of erythroid precursors, or >=5% if SF3B1 mutated, defines MDS with ring sideroblasts).
Conventional G-banded cytogenetics: karyotype of >=20 metaphases (detects del(5q), monosomy 7/del(7q), trisomy 8, complex karyotype with >=3 abnormalities).
Comprehensive targeted myeloid NGS panel: testing for SF3B1, TP53 (essential to determine single vs multi-hit allelic state), ASXL1, RUNX1, STAG2, U2AF1, SRSF2, EZH2, IDH1/IDH2, DNMT3A, TET2.
Laboratory baseline: serum erythropoietin (EPO) level drawn prior to red cell transfusions, ferritin, iron panel, vitamin B12, folate, TSH.

nodes.name: IPSS risk
nodes.title: Prognostic risk stratification (IPSS-M / IPSS-R)
nodes.description: Assign risk with the Molecular IPSS (preferred) supported by the revised IPSS. Risk group determines lower-risk versus higher-risk management.
bullets: Lower risk: IPSS-M Very Low / Low / Moderate-Low, or IPSS-R <=3.5
Higher risk: IPSS-M Moderate-High / High / Very High, or IPSS-R >3.5

nodes.name: Lower-risk cytogenetics
nodes.title: Lower-risk MDS: del(5q) status
nodes.description: Lower-risk MDS branches first on isolated del(5q), which has a dedicated Category 1 preferred therapy.
bullets: Isolated del(5q) with or without one other cytogenetic abnormality, excluding monosomy 7/del(7q)
Non-del(5q): all other lower-risk cytogenetics

options.label: Isolated del(5q) (+/- one other abnormality, excluding monosomy 7/del(7q))

nodes.name: Anemia triage
nodes.title: Non-del(5q) lower-risk MDS: anemia triage
nodes.description: For non-del(5q) lower-risk disease, the next therapy is chosen by serum EPO, ring sideroblast status, transfusion burden, and prior ESA response.
bullets: Serum EPO <=500 mU/mL with low transfusion burden favors erythropoiesis-stimulating agents
Ring sideroblasts >=15% (or >=5% with SF3B1 mutation) or high transfusion burden favors luspatercept
Prior ESA/luspatercept failure moves to imetelstat or a hypomethylating agent

options.label: Serum EPO <=500 mU/mL, low transfusion burden, ESA-naive
Ring sideroblasts positive (>=15%, or >=5% with SF3B1) or high transfusion burden

nodes.name: Lenalidomide
nodes.title: Lower-risk del(5q) MDS: lenalidomide
nodes.description: Category 1 preferred therapy for lower-risk isolated del(5q) MDS with symptomatic anemia.
nodes.path: Myelodysplastic Syndromes / Lower Risk / del(5q) / Lenalidomide
bullets: Lenalidomide 10 mg PO daily x 21 days q28d (Category 1 Preferred); approximately 67% of patients achieve transfusion independence.
Monitor CBC weekly for neutropenia and thrombocytopenia; dose-hold and dose-reduce per cytopenias.
Assess transfusion burden and cytogenetic response at 2-4 cycles; continue until progression or intolerance.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.

nodes.name: ESA
nodes.title: Lower-risk non-del(5q) MDS: erythropoiesis-stimulating agents
nodes.description: ESA therapy for non-del(5q) lower-risk MDS with symptomatic anemia and serum EPO <=500 mU/mL.
nodes.path: Myelodysplastic Syndromes / Lower Risk / Anemia / ESA
bullets: Epoetin alfa 40,000-60,000 U SC weekly, or darbepoetin alfa 150-300 mcg SC q1-2w, with or without G-CSF.
Confirm serum EPO <=500 mU/mL drawn before transfusions; ESA response is unlikely above this threshold.
Replenish iron, B12, and folate before judging response; assess hemoglobin and transfusion need at 6-8 weeks.
Non-responders advance to luspatercept (if ring sideroblasts positive) or imetelstat / HMA pathways.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.

nodes.name: Luspatercept
nodes.title: Lower-risk MDS: luspatercept for RS-positive or transfusion-dependent anemia
nodes.description: Luspatercept for transfusion-dependent lower-risk MDS with ring sideroblasts or ESA-refractory disease (COMMANDS Category 1 Preferred).
nodes.path: Myelodysplastic Syndromes / Lower Risk / Anemia / Luspatercept
bullets: Luspatercept 1.0 mg/kg SC q3w, titrating to 1.33 mg/kg then 1.75 mg/kg for inadequate response (COMMANDS Category 1 Preferred, with superior durability over ESAs).
Indicated for ring sideroblasts >=15% (or >=5% with SF3B1 mutation), ESA-refractory disease, or high baseline transfusion burden.
Monitor pre-dose hemoglobin, blood pressure, and for thromboembolic symptoms; hold for hemoglobin above target per label.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.

nodes.name: Imetelstat or HMA
nodes.title: Lower-risk MDS refractory to ESA / luspatercept: imetelstat or HMA
nodes.description: Options for ESA/luspatercept-refractory transfusion-dependent lower-risk MDS, including high baseline transfusion burden.
nodes.path: Myelodysplastic Syndromes / Lower Risk / Anemia / Refractory
bullets: Imetelstat 7.1 mg/kg IV q4w, a telomerase inhibitor studied in the IMerge trial for ESA-refractory transfusion-dependent lower-risk MDS (monitor LFTs and cytopenias).
Hypomethylating agent alternative: azacitidine 75 mg/m2 SC/IV daily x 7 days q28d, or decitabine 20 mg/m2 IV daily x 5 days.
Clinical trial enrollment is preferred where available before committing to chronic HMA therapy.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.

nodes.name: HCT candidacy
nodes.title: Higher-risk MDS: allogeneic HCT candidacy and disease course
nodes.description: Higher-risk MDS management hinges on fitness for allogeneic HCT, the only curative modality, and on whether disease is relapsed or refractory.
bullets: Fit candidates: prompt donor search with HMA bridging to reduce marrow blasts below 5% before HCT
Non-candidates: definitive hypomethylating agent therapy
Relapsed or refractory after HMA: clinical trial or AML-like therapy

nodes.name: HCT with HMA bridging
nodes.title: Higher-risk MDS: allogeneic HCT with HMA bridging
nodes.description: Curative-intent pathway for fit higher-risk MDS: urgent transplant referral with hypomethylating bridging.
nodes.path: Myelodysplastic Syndromes / Higher Risk / HCT Candidate
bullets: Prompt HLA typing and donor search at diagnosis; HCT is the only curative modality for MDS.
HMA bridging to reduce marrow blasts below 5% prior to allogeneic HCT: azacitidine 75 mg/m2 IV/SC d1-7 q28d (Category 1), or decitabine 20 mg/m2 IV d1-5.
Reassess marrow blast percentage and donor availability each cycle; proceed to conditioning without delay once blasts are controlled.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.

nodes.name: HMA definitive
nodes.title: Higher-risk MDS, non-HCT candidate: hypomethylating agent therapy
nodes.description: Definitive HMA therapy for higher-risk MDS in patients who are not allogeneic HCT candidates.
nodes.path: Myelodysplastic Syndromes / Higher Risk / Non-HCT / HMA
bullets: Azacitidine 75 mg/m2 IV/SC d1-7 q28d (Category 1 with demonstrated overall survival benefit), or decitabine 20 mg/m2 IV d1-5, or oral decitabine/cedazuridine (Inqovi) where parenteral therapy is not feasible.
Continue a minimum of 4-6 cycles before judging response; responders continue until progression or intolerance.
Monitor CBC, renal function, and transfusion burden each cycle; provide infection prophylaxis per neutropenia.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.

nodes.name: R/R after HMA
nodes.title: Higher-risk MDS relapsed / refractory: trial or AML-like therapy
nodes.description: Salvage pathway for higher-risk MDS that is relapsed or refractory after hypomethylating therapy.
bullets: Clinical trial enrollment is preferred (HMA plus venetoclax combinations or novel agents).
HMA plus venetoclax where a trial is unavailable and marrow blast burden supports it.
Intensive AML-like induction for fit patients with rising blasts approaching AML.
Best supportive care and goals-of-care discussion for patients unfit for salvage therapy.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
